answer.rationale: The write-path latency degradation is confined to the primary region, mirroring the conditions in memory_b2 where regional failover restored latency quickly with clean traffic shift and error-rate recovery within minutes. Rolling back the release is prohibited by compliance (security patch cannot be reverted), eliminating rollback_release. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) address dependency/partner outages, not intra-region write-path latency. Routing to read replicas (memory_b5) offloads reads, but the current problem is on the write path with heavy settlement traffic, so it would not resolve the core issue. Adding capacity could help but takes time to provision and doesn't address a region-specific degradation pattern as decisively as shifting traffic away from the impaired primary. Staged release gating (memory_b6) is a preventive control, not an active incident mitigation. Regional failover directly moves the degraded write path to a healthy region, preserves all customer writes (no rollback, no dropped transactions), and aligns with the inherited record showing this intervention works well under comparable conditions. The one memory I want verified is memory_b2, to confirm the original incident details—specifically whether the failover was clean under high write volume, which is the closest analog to today's settlement-peak load.
